author: Augustine
source_text: illae quibus tenere cogebar Aeneae nescio cuius errores, oblitus errorum meorum, et plorare Didonem mortuam, quia se occidit ab amore.
question: Cuius reginae mortem, quae se ab amore occidit, Augustinus puer in schola legens flebat?
question_en: Over which queen's death, who killed herself out of love, did the boy Augustine weep as he read in school?
derivation: The celebrated detail of Conf. 1: the boy wept over Dido's death ('plorare Didonem mortuam, quia se occidit ab amore'). Anchored to Augustine + the named queen Dido; the question's description (a queen who killed herself for love) alone fixes the referent. Single-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book (one of the most-quoted episodes in the Confessions).

author: Augustine
source_text: illae quibus tenere cogebar Aeneae nescio cuius errores, oblitus errorum meorum, et plorare Didonem mortuam, quia se occidit ab amore.
question: Cuius viri errores Augustinus puer in schola ediscere cogebatur?
question_en: Whose wanderings was the boy Augustine forced to learn by heart in school?
derivation: The wandering hero whose 'errores' Augustine was compelled to memorize is named in the text ('Aeneae nescio cuius errores'). Entity-anchored to Augustine's schooling + the named hero Aeneas; single-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book autobiographical fact.

author: Augustine
source_text: quid autem erat causae cur graecas litteras oderam, quibus puerulus imbuebar? ne nunc quidem mihi satis exploratum est. adamaveram enim latinas, non quas primi magistri sed quas docent qui grammatici vocantur.
question: Cum latinas litteras adamavisset, quas litteras Augustinus puer se odisse confitetur?
question_en: Although he had come to love Latin letters, which letters does Augustine confess he hated as a boy?
derivation: The well-known biographical fact that Augustine loved Latin but hated Greek as a schoolboy ('cur graecas litteras oderam ... adamaveram enim latinas'). Anchored to Augustine + the two named languages; clean which-language answer supported verbatim. Indirect statement 'se odisse' under 'confitetur'; concessive cum-clause with pluperfect subjunctive 'adamavisset'. Closed-book (Augustine's poor Greek is a standard fact about him).

author: Augustine
source_text: proponebatur enim mihi negotium, animae meae satis inquietum praemio laudis et dedecoris vel plagarum metu, ut dicerem verba Iunonis irascentis et dolentis quod non posset Italia Teucrorum avertere regem, quae numquam Iunonem dixisse audieram.
question: Cuius deae verba, irascentis et dolentis quod Teucrorum regem ab Italia avertere non posset, Augustino puero in schola dicenda proponebantur?
question_en: Whose words — those of a goddess angry and grieving that she could not turn the king of the Trojans away from Italy — was the boy Augustine set in school to declaim?
derivation: Augustine's school declamation exercise: putting into prose the angry speech of a goddess who could not keep the Trojan king from Italy ('verba Iunonis irascentis et dolentis quod non posset Italia Teucrorum avertere regem'). The description alone determines Juno (the Aeneid's divine antagonist), making it closed-book via both the Confessions and basic mythology. Single-name answer supported verbatim; anchored to Augustine's schooling + the named goddess and the Teucri/Italia.

author: Augustine
source_text: veni Carthaginem, et circumstrepebat me undique sartago flagitiosorum amorum.
question: In quam urbem Augustinus adulescens venit, ubi studiis eloquentiae operam dabat?
question_en: Into what city did the young Augustine come, where he was devoting himself to the study of eloquence?
derivation: The opening words of Book 3, 'veni Carthaginem.' Anchored to Augustine + his studies (he studies eloquence/rhetoric there, 3.3.6 'in schola rhetoris', 3.4.7 'discebam libros eloquentiae'); single place-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book: Augustine's student years at Carthage are a famous biographical fact.

author: Augustine
source_text: et usitato iam discendi ordine perveneram in librum cuiusdam Ciceronis, cuius linguam fere omnes mirantur, pectus non ita. sed liber ille ipsius exhortationem continet ad philosophiam et vocatur 'Hortensius'. ille vero liber mutavit affectum meum.
question: Quo titulo inscribitur liber Ciceronis quo lecto Augustinus ad amorem sapientiae accensus est?
question_en: Under what title is the book of Cicero, on reading which Augustine was kindled to the love of wisdom, inscribed?
derivation: Cicero's (now lost) Hortensius, an exhortation to philosophy, changed Augustine and inflamed him to wisdom ('liber ille ipsius exhortationem continet ad philosophiam et vocatur Hortensius. ille vero liber mutavit affectum meum'). Anchored to Cicero + Augustine; single title answer supported verbatim. Closed-book: one of the most famous turning points in the Confessions.

author: Augustine
source_text: et usitato iam discendi ordine perveneram in librum cuiusdam Ciceronis, cuius linguam fere omnes mirantur, pectus non ita. sed liber ille ipsius exhortationem continet ad philosophiam et vocatur 'Hortensius'. ille vero liber mutavit affectum meum.
question: Cuius auctoris liber, exhortationem ad philosophiam continens, Augustinum ad sapientiae studium accendit?
question_en: Which author's book, containing an exhortation to philosophy, kindled Augustine to the pursuit of wisdom?
derivation: The book that inflamed Augustine to philosophy is by Cicero ('perveneram in librum cuiusdam Ciceronis... exhortationem continet ad philosophiam'). Anchored to Augustine + the Hortensius; single-name answer supported verbatim. Distinct fact (the author) from the work's title; closed-book.

author: Augustine
source_text: non enim ad acuendam linguam, quod videbar emere maternis mercedibus, cum agerem annum aetatis undevicensimum iam defuncto patre ante biennium, non ergo ad acuendam linguam referebam illum librum.
question: Quotum annum aetatis agebat Augustinus cum librum Ciceronis Hortensium legeret?
question_en: What year of his age was Augustine in when he read Cicero's book the Hortensius?
derivation: Number fact: Augustine read the Hortensius in the nineteenth year of his age ('cum agerem annum aetatis undevicensimum'). Anchored to Augustine + the reading of the Hortensius; short, verifiable answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Augustine
source_text: et credidi miser magis esse misericordiam praestandam fructibus terrae quam hominibus propter quos nascerentur. si quis enim esuriens peteret qui manichaeus non esset, quasi capitali supplicio damnanda buccella videretur si ei daretur.
question: Cuius haereticae sectae asseclam se Augustinus adulescens per plures annos fuisse confitetur?
question_en: Of what heretical sect does Augustine confess that he was a follower for several years as a young man?
derivation: Augustine names the Manichees while describing his own former belief that food should be given only to a Manichee ('si quis... qui manichaeus non esset...'); the Manichee period dominates the latter half of Book 3. Anchored to Augustine; single-name answer supported by 'manichaeus'. Closed-book: Augustine's years as a Manichee are among the most famous facts of his life. (Indirect statement 'se... asseclam fuisse' governed by 'confitetur'.)

author: Augustine
source_text: nam novem ferme anni secuti sunt quibus ego in illo limo profundi ac tenebris falsitatis, cum saepe surgere conarer et gravius alliderer, volutatus sum.
question: Per quot fere annos Augustinus in errore Manichaeorum versatus est?
question_en: For about how many years was Augustine entangled in the error of the Manichees?
derivation: Number fact: 'novem ferme anni secuti sunt' in which Augustine was mired in falsity — the Manichee error that is the subject of Book 3. Answer mirrors the approximative 'ferme'. Anchored to Augustine + the Manichees; short, verifiable. Closed-book: the roughly nine years as a Manichee are a famous biographical datum.

author: Augustine
source_text: vidit enim se stantem in quadam regula lignea et advenientem ad se iuvenem splendidum hilarem atque arridentem sibi, cum illa esset maerens et maerore confecta.
question: In qua re Monica, mater Augustini, se stantem per somnium vidit, cum iuvenis splendidus ad eam accederet?
question_en: On what did Monica, Augustine's mother, see herself standing in a dream, as a radiant young man approached her?
derivation: Monica's famous consolatory dream: she sees herself standing on a wooden rule ('se stantem in quadam regula lignea') when a radiant youth tells her that where she is, there her son will also be. Anchored to Monica (Augustine's mother, well known though unnamed in this book) + the dream; short answer supported verbatim. Closed-book: the dream of Monica is a celebrated episode.

author: Augustine
source_text: ille iam substomachans taedio, 'vade' inquit 'a me. ita vivas: fieri non potest, ut filius istarum lacrimarum pereat.'
question: Quibus verbis episcopus quidam Monicam, Augustini matrem, de filii salute consolatus est?
answer: Fieri non potest, ut filius istarum lacrimarum pereat.
question_en: With what words did a certain bishop console Monica, Augustine's mother, concerning her son's salvation?
answer_en: It cannot be that the son of these tears should perish.
derivation: The famous consoling saying of the (unnamed) bishop to the weeping Monica. Anchored to Monica (Augustine's mother) + the bishop; the answer is the famous quoted sentence supported verbatim. Closed-book: among the most-quoted lines of the Confessions. Kept as a short famous quotation per the task; the bishop himself is unnamed in the text ('quendam episcopum').

author: Augustine
source_text: iam venerat Carthaginem quidam manichaeorum episcopus, Faustus nomine, magnus laqueus diaboli, et multi implicabantur in eo per inlecebram suaviloquentiae.
question: Quo nomine appellabatur ille Manichaeorum episcopus qui Carthaginem venit, quem Augustinus diu venturum expectabat?
question_en: By what name was that Manichaean bishop who came to Carthage, whom Augustine long awaited, called?
derivation: The Manichee bishop whose arrival at Carthage dominates Book 5 is named verbatim: 'manichaeorum episcopus, Faustus nomine.' Anchored to the Manichees + Carthage + Augustine's long expectation; single-name answer. Closed-book: Faustus is famous (Augustine later wrote Contra Faustum Manichaeum).

author: Augustine
source_text: iam venerat Carthaginem quidam manichaeorum episcopus, Faustus nomine, magnus laqueus diaboli.
question: Cuius sectae episcopus erat Faustus, quem Augustinus Carthagini audivit?
question_en: Of what sect was Faustus, whom Augustine heard at Carthage, a bishop?
derivation: Faustus is identified as a bishop of the Manichees ('manichaeorum episcopus, Faustus nomine'). Anchored to Faustus by name; single-answer (the sect/office), distinct from the name fact. Closed-book biographical fact.

author: Augustine
source_text: proloquar in conspectu dei mei annum illum undetricensimum aetatis meae. iam venerat Carthaginem quidam manichaeorum episcopus, Faustus nomine, magnus laqueus diaboli.
question: Quoto anno aetatis suae Augustinus Faustum Carthaginem venisse narrat?
question_en: In which year of his age does Augustine relate that Faustus came to Carthage?
derivation: Augustine opens by declaring the year he is narrating, his 29th ('annum illum undetricensimum aetatis meae'), in which Faustus had come to Carthage. Number fact anchored to Augustine + Faustus's arrival; undetricensimus = 29th. Short, verifiable; age facts are precedent (cf. conf9).

author: Augustine
source_text: et per annos ferme ipsos novem quibus eos animo vagabundus audivi nimis extento desiderio venturum expectabam istum Faustum.
question: Per quot fere annos Augustinus Manichaeos audiverat, dum Faustum venturum expectabat?
question_en: For about how many years had Augustine been listening to the Manichees while he awaited the coming of Faustus?
derivation: Number fact: Augustine had heard the Manichees for about nine years, awaiting Faustus ('per annos ferme ipsos novem... audivi... expectabam istum Faustum'). Answer mirrors the approximative 'ferme.' Anchored to Augustine + Manichees + Faustus. Closed-book: his ~9 years as a Manichaean auditor is standard biography.

author: Augustine
source_text: egisti ergo mecum ut mihi persuaderetur Romam pergere et potius ibi docere quod docebam Carthagini.
question: Quo Augustinus ex Carthagine docendi causa transiit?
question_en: Where did Augustine cross over to from Carthage for the sake of teaching?
derivation: Augustine was persuaded to leave Carthage (where he taught) and go to Rome to teach there ('Romam pergere et potius ibi docere quod docebam Carthagini'). Anchored to Augustine + Carthage; single place answer. Closed-book: his move from Carthage to Rome is canonical biography.

author: Augustine
source_text: et ecce excipior ibi flagello aegritudinis corporalis, et ibam iam ad inferos portans omnia mala quae commiseram et in te et in me et in alios.
question: In qua urbe Augustinus, mox ut eo ex Africa pervenit, gravi corporis aegritudine correptus est?
question_en: In what city was Augustine struck down by a grave bodily illness soon after he arrived there from Africa?
derivation: On reaching Rome from Africa, Augustine was seized by bodily illness ('excipior ibi flagello aegritudinis corporalis'; the 'ibi' is Rome, where he had just sailed from Carthage). Anchored to Augustine + Rome + arrival from Africa; single place answer. Closed-book: his near-fatal illness at Rome is a known episode.

author: Augustine
source_text: itaque posteaquam missum est a Mediolanio Romam ad praefectum urbis, ut illi civitati rhetoricae magister provideretur, impertita etiam evectione publica, ego ipse ambivi per eos ipsos manichaeis vanitatibus ebrios (quibus ut carerem ibam, sed utrique nesciebamus) ut dictione proposita me probatum praefectus tunc Symmachus mitteret.
question: Quis praefectus urbis Augustinum Mediolanium misit, ut illic rhetoricam doceret?
question_en: Which prefect of the City sent Augustine to Milan to teach rhetoric there?
derivation: The prefect of Rome, Symmachus, having approved Augustine by a set declamation, sent him to Milan ('praefectus tunc Symmachus mitteret'). Anchored to the prefecture of Rome + Milan + Augustine; single-name answer. Closed-book: Q. Aurelius Symmachus is a well-known figure.

author: Augustine
source_text: itaque posteaquam missum est a Mediolanio Romam ad praefectum urbis, ut illi civitati rhetoricae magister provideretur, impertita etiam evectione publica, ego ipse ambivi per eos ipsos manichaeis vanitatibus ebrios (quibus ut carerem ibam, sed utrique nesciebamus) ut dictione proposita me probatum praefectus tunc Symmachus mitteret. et veni Mediolanium ad Ambrosium episcopum, in optimis notum orbi terrae, pium cultorem tuum.
question: Quo Augustinus, a Symmacho praefecto probatus, rhetoricae magister missus est?
question_en: Where was Augustine sent as a teacher of rhetoric after being approved by the prefect Symmachus?
derivation: Milan had asked Rome's prefect to provide it a teacher of rhetoric ('a Mediolanio... ut illi civitati rhetoricae magister provideretur'); Symmachus sent Augustine, who 'veni Mediolanium.' Anchored to Augustine + Symmachus + the office of rhetoric-master; single place answer (Mediolanium). Closed-book: his professorship at Milan is standard biography.

author: Augustine
source_text: et veni Mediolanium ad Ambrosium episcopum, in optimis notum orbi terrae, pium cultorem tuum, cuius tunc eloquia strenue ministrabant adipem frumenti tui et laetitiam olei et sobriam vini ebrietatem populo tuo.
question: Ad quem episcopum Augustinus Mediolanium veniens accessit?
question_en: To which bishop did Augustine come on arriving at Milan?
derivation: On reaching Milan Augustine came to its bishop Ambrose ('et veni Mediolanium ad Ambrosium episcopum'). Anchored to Augustine + Milan; single-name answer. Closed-book: Ambrose of Milan and his role in Augustine's conversion are famous.

author: Augustine
source_text: et studiose audiebam disputantem in populo, non intentione qua debui, sed quasi explorans eius facundiam, utrum conveniret famae suae an maior minorve proflueret quam praedicabatur.
question: Quid potissimum in Ambrosio Augustinus primo explorabat, cum eum in populo disputantem audiret?
question_en: What above all did Augustine at first examine in Ambrose when he heard him preaching to the people?
derivation: Augustine eagerly listened to Ambrose preaching to the people, at first attending to his eloquence rather than the content ('quasi explorans eius facundiam'; 'rerum autem incuriosus'). Anchored to Augustine + Ambrose; short answer (his eloquence/facundia) supported verbatim. Fact-seeking and closed-book: the well-known point that Augustine first came for Ambrose's rhetoric.

author: Augustine
source_text: ubi autem commemoravi legisse me quosdam libros platonicorum, quos Victorinus, quondam rhetor urbis Romae, quem christianum defunctum esse audieram, in latinam linguam transtulisset, gratulatus est mihi quod non in aliorum philosophorum scripta incidissem plena fallaciarum et deceptionum secundum elementa huius mundi.
question: Quis libros platonicorum, quos Augustinus legerat, in latinam linguam transtulit?
question_en: Who translated into Latin the books of the Platonists that Augustine had read?
derivation: Augustine recounts to Simplicianus that he had read certain Platonist books which Victorinus, once a rhetor of the city of Rome, had translated into Latin. Anchored to the libri platonicorum + Latin; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'quos Victorinus ... in latinam linguam transtulisset.' Closed-book: Marius Victorinus's Latin renderings of the Neoplatonists are a well-known fact of intellectual history.

author: Augustine
source_text: doctor tot nobilium senatorum, qui etiam ob insigne praeclari magisterii, quod cives huius mundi eximium putant, statuam Romano foro meruerat et acceperat.
question: In quo loco Victorinus rhetor, ob praeclarum magisterium, statuam meruit et accepit?
question_en: In what place did Victorinus the rhetor earn and receive a statue, on account of his distinguished teaching?
derivation: Victorinus, teacher of many noble senators, earned and received a statue in the Roman forum for his eminent teaching of rhetoric. Anchored to Victorinus the rhetor; place answer supported verbatim by 'statuam Romano foro meruerat et acceperat.' Closed-book biographical detail (his statue in the forum is a famous mark of his standing as rhetor at Rome).

author: Augustine
source_text: sed ubi mihi homo tuus Simplicianus de Victorino ista narravit, exarsi ad imitandum: ad hoc enim et ille narraverat.
question: Quis Augustino de conversione Victorini rhetoris narravit?
question_en: Who recounted to Augustine the conversion of Victorinus the rhetor?
derivation: It was Simplicianus who told Augustine the story of Victorinus's conversion, precisely to spur him to imitate it. Anchored to Augustine + Victorinus; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'Simplicianus de Victorino ista narravit.' Closed-book (Simplicianus, later bishop of Milan, is a recognized figure in the conversion narrative).

author: Augustine
source_text: posteaquam vero et illud addidit, quod imperatoris Iuliani temporibus lege data prohibiti sunt christiani docere litteraturam et oratoriam. quam legem ille amplexus, loquacem scholam deserere maluit.
question: Cuius imperatoris temporibus christiani lege data docere litteraturam et oratoriam prohibiti sunt?
question_en: In which emperor's reign were Christians forbidden by a law to teach literature and rhetoric?
derivation: Augustine reports that under the emperor Julian a law forbade Christians to teach literature and rhetoric, a law Victorinus embraced by leaving his school. Anchored to the school-teaching ban; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'imperatoris Iuliani temporibus lege data prohibiti sunt christiani docere litteraturam et oratoriam.' Closed-book (Julian's edict on teachers, AD 362, is established Roman history).

author: Augustine
source_text: cui ego cum indicassem illis me scripturis curam maximam impendere, ortus est sermo ipso narrante de Antonio Aegyptio monacho, cuius nomen excellenter clarebat apud servos tuos, nos autem usque in illam horam latebat.
question: Quis, cum in domum Augustini et Alypii venisset, eis de Antonio Aegyptio monacho narravit?
question_en: Who, having come to the house of Augustine and Alypius, told them about Antony the Egyptian monk?
derivation: The teller ('ipso narrante') is Ponticianus, named at the opening of 8.6.14 ('ad nos domum venit ad me et Alypium Ponticianus quidam ... praeclare in palatio militans'). Anchored to Augustine + Alypius + Antony; single-name answer. Closed-book: Ponticianus's visit is the famous trigger of Augustine's conversion.

author: Augustine
source_text: ortus est sermo ipso narrante de Antonio Aegyptio monacho, cuius nomen excellenter clarebat apud servos tuos, nos autem usque in illam horam latebat.
question: Quo nomine appellatur monachus Aegyptius de quo Ponticianus apud Augustinum narravit?
question_en: By what name is the Egyptian monk called about whom Ponticianus spoke at Augustine's house?
derivation: Ponticianus's conversation turned to Antony, the Egyptian monk. Anchored to Ponticianus + Egyptian monk; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'de Antonio Aegyptio monacho.' Closed-book (Antony of Egypt is among the most famous of the early monks).

author: Augustine
source_text: sed illos vagabundos inruisse in quandam casam ubi habitabant quidam servi tui spiritu pauperes, qualium est regnum caelorum, et invenisse ibi codicem in quo scripta erat vita Antonii. quam legere coepit unus eorum et mirari et accendi, et inter legendum meditari arripere talem vitam et relicta militia saeculari servire tibi. erant autem ex eis quos dicunt agentes in rebus.
question: Cuius vita scripta erat in codice quem agentes in rebus, Ponticiani contubernales, reppererunt, quo lecto militiam saecularem reliquerunt?
question_en: Whose life was written in the codex that the agentes in rebus, Ponticianus's companions, found, and which, once read, made them abandon their worldly service?
derivation: Two of Ponticianus's fellow court officials ('agentes in rebus') found in a cottage a codex containing the Life of Antony, and reading it abandoned their imperial careers. Anchored to the officials + the codex; answer supported verbatim by 'codicem in quo scripta erat vita Antonii.' Closed-book (the role of Athanasius's Vita Antonii in these conversions is a famous episode).

author: Augustine
source_text: et ecce audio vocem de vicina domo cum cantu dicentis et crebro repetentis, quasi pueri an puellae, nescio: 'tolle lege, tolle lege.'
question: Quae verba Augustinus, in horto sedens, a voce quasi pueri vel puellae de vicina domo crebro repeti audivit?
question_en: What words did Augustine, sitting in the garden, hear repeated again and again by a voice as of a boy or girl from a neighboring house?
derivation: The famous chant that prompted Augustine to open the apostle's codex. Anchored to Augustine + the garden scene; the quoted words are supported verbatim by "'tolle lege, tolle lege.'" Closed-book (one of the most famous moments in the Confessions) and translatable ('take up and read').

author: Augustine
source_text: et forte supra mensam lusoriam quae ante nos erat attendit codicem. tulit, aperuit, invenit apostolum Paulum, inopinate sane: putaverat enim aliquid de libris quorum professio me conterebat.
question: Cuius apostoli scripta continebat codex, quem Ponticianus in domo Augustini aperuit et quem Augustinus postea in horto arripuit ac legit?
question_en: Whose apostolic writings did the codex contain, which Ponticianus opened in Augustine's house and which Augustine afterward seized and read in the garden?
derivation: The codex on the gaming table that Ponticianus opened proved to contain 'apostolum Paulum'; it is the same 'codicem apostoli' Augustine seized and read at his conversion (8.12.29, Rom. 13:13-14). Anchored to Augustine; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'invenit apostolum Paulum.' Closed-book (Augustine's conversion reading of Paul is famous).

author: Augustine
source_text: itaque concitus redii in eum locum ubi sedebat Alypius: ibi enim posueram codicem apostoli cum inde surrexeram. arripui, aperui, et legi in silentio capitulum quo primum coniecti sunt oculi mei.
question: Quis amicus una cum Augustino in horto sedebat quo tempore, codice apostoli arripto, ad fidem conversus est?
question_en: Which friend was sitting with Augustine in the garden at the time when, having seized the apostle's codex, he was converted to the faith?
derivation: Alypius was beside Augustine throughout the garden scene ('Alypius affixus lateri meo' 8.11.27; 'ubi sedebat Alypius' 8.12.29; 'indicavi Alypio' 8.12.30) and converted with him. Anchored to Augustine + the garden conversion; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'redii in eum locum ubi sedebat Alypius.' Closed-book (Alypius is Augustine's well-known companion).

author: Augustine
source_text: pariter remeabamus in Africam. et cum apud Ostia Tiberina essemus, mater defuncta est.
question: In quo loco mater Augustini mortua est, cum in Africam redire pararent?
question_en: In what place did Augustine's mother die, as they were preparing to return to Africa?
derivation: Canonical fact of Book 9: Monica dies at Ostia as the party heads back to Africa. Anchored to Augustine + his mother + the return to Africa; single place answer supported verbatim by 'cum apud Ostia Tiberina essemus, mater defuncta est.' Closed-book, one of the most famous deaths in the Confessions.

author: Augustine
source_text: ut quotquot haec legerint, meminerint ad altare tuum Monnicae, famulae tuae, cum Patricio, quondam eius coniuge, per quorum carnem introduxisti me in hanc vitam, quemadmodum nescio.
question: Quo nomine appellatur mater Augustini, quae apud Ostia mortua est?
question_en: By what name is Augustine's mother, who died at Ostia, called?
derivation: Augustine names his mother only here at the close of Book 9. Anchored to Augustine + his mother; single-name answer supported by 'Monnicae, famulae tuae... per quorum carnem introduxisti me in hanc vitam.' Closed-book (Monica is among the most famous mothers in literature). Spelling 'Monnica' per the text (also Monica).

author: Augustine
source_text: ut quotquot haec legerint, meminerint ad altare tuum Monnicae, famulae tuae, cum Patricio, quondam eius coniuge, per quorum carnem introduxisti me in hanc vitam, quemadmodum nescio.
question: Quo nomine appellatur pater Augustini, maritus Monnicae?
question_en: By what name is Augustine's father, the husband of Monnica, called?
derivation: Patricius is named as Monnica's husband and Augustine's parent ('cum Patricio, quondam eius coniuge, per quorum carnem introduxisti me'). Anchored to Augustine + Monnica; single-name answer. Also named at 9.9.19. Closed-book biographical fact.

author: Augustine
source_text: adiunximus etiam nobis puerum Adeodatum ex me natum carnaliter de peccato meo. tu bene feceras eum.
question: Quo nomine appellatur filius quem Augustinus carnaliter genuit?
question_en: By what name is the son whom Augustine begot in the flesh called?
derivation: Augustine's natural son, joined to the group and baptized with him and Alypius at Milan. Anchored to Augustine; single-name answer supported verbatim by 'puerum Adeodatum ex me natum carnaliter.' Closed-book.

author: Augustine
source_text: adiunximus etiam nobis puerum Adeodatum ex me natum carnaliter de peccato meo. tu bene feceras eum. annorum erat ferme quindecim et ingenio praeveniebat multos graves et doctos viros.
question: Quot fere annos natus erat Adeodatus, Augustini filius, eo tempore quo baptizatus est?
question_en: About how many years old was Adeodatus, Augustine's son, at the time he was baptized?
derivation: Number fact anchored to Adeodatus (Augustine's son) at the time of the Milan baptism. Answer mirrors the source's approximative 'ferme' ('annorum erat ferme quindecim'). Short, verifiable, closed-book.

author: Augustine
source_text: est liber noster qui inscribitur 'de magistro': ipse ibi mecum loquitur. tu scis illius esse sensa omnia quae inseruntur ibi ex persona conlocutoris mei, cum esset in annis sedecim.
question: Quo titulo inscribitur liber Augustini in quo filius eius Adeodatus conlocutor inducitur?
question_en: Under what title is the book of Augustine in which his son Adeodatus is brought in as interlocutor inscribed?
derivation: Augustine states that in his dialogue De magistro the interlocutor's words are his son's ('ex persona conlocutoris mei'). Anchored to Augustine + Adeodatus; single title answer supported verbatim. Closed-book (De Magistro is a well-known work).

author: Augustine
source_text: relicto rure Mediolanium remeavimus. placuit et Alypio renasci in te mecum iam induto humilitate sacramentis tuis congrua et fortissimo domitori corporis, usque ad Italicum solum glaciale nudo pede obterendum insolito ausu.
question: Quis amicus Augustini una cum eo Mediolani baptizatus est?
question_en: Which friend of Augustine was baptized at Milan together with him?
derivation: Alypius decided to be 'reborn' (baptized) along with Augustine on their return to Milan ('relicto rure Mediolanium remeavimus. placuit et Alypio renasci in te mecum'). Anchored to Augustine + Milan; single-name answer. Closed-book (Alypius is Augustine's well-known companion).

author: Augustine
source_text: et insinuavi per litteras antistiti tuo, viro sancto Ambrosio, pristinos errores meos et praesens votum meum, ut moneret quid mihi potissimum de libris tuis legendum esset, quo percipiendae tantae gratiae paratior aptiorque fierem. at ille iussit Esaiam prophetam, credo, quod prae ceteris evangelii vocationisque gentium sit praenuntiator apertior.
question: Quem prophetam Augustino legendum antistes Ambrosius iussit?
question_en: Which prophet did the bishop Ambrose order Augustine to read?
derivation: Augustine asked the bishop Ambrose what to read; Ambrose directed him to Isaiah ('at ille iussit Esaiam prophetam'). Anchored to Ambrose (named 'antistiti tuo, viro sancto Ambrosio') + Augustine; single-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book.

author: Augustine
source_text: ergo die nono aegritudinis suae, quinquagesimo et sexto anno aetatis suae, tricesimo et tertio aetatis meae, anima illa religiosa et pia corpore soluta est.
question: Quoto anno aetatis suae Monnica, mater Augustini, mortua est?
question_en: In which year of her age did Monnica, Augustine's mother, die?
derivation: Number fact anchored to Monnica: she died in the 56th year of her age ('quinquagesimo et sexto anno aetatis suae'). Short, verifiable, closed-book.

author: Augustine
source_text: ergo die nono aegritudinis suae, quinquagesimo et sexto anno aetatis suae, tricesimo et tertio aetatis meae, anima illa religiosa et pia corpore soluta est.
question: Quotum annum aetatis agebat Augustinus cum mater eius Monnica mortua est?
question_en: What year of his age was Augustine in when his mother Monnica died?
derivation: Number fact anchored to Augustine: he was in his 33rd year at his mother's death ('tricesimo et tertio aetatis meae'). Distinct referent from the mother's age; short, verifiable, closed-book.

author: Augustine
source_text: ergo die nono aegritudinis suae, quinquagesimo et sexto anno aetatis suae, tricesimo et tertio aetatis meae, anima illa religiosa et pia corpore soluta est.
question: Quoto die aegritudinis suae Monnica mortua est?
question_en: On which day of her illness did Monnica die?
derivation: Number fact anchored to Monnica: she died on the ninth day of her illness ('die nono aegritudinis suae'). Short, verifiable, closed-book. (Note 9.11.27's 'vix intra quinque dies... decubuit febribus' refers to the acute febrile phase; the explicit death-statement gives the ninth day of the whole illness.)

author: Augustine
source_text: tunc memorato antistiti tuo per visum aperuisti quo loco laterent martyrum corpora Protasii et Gervasii, quae per tot annos incorrupta in thesauro secreti tui reconderas, unde opportune promeres ad cohercendam rabiem femineam sed regiam.
question: Quorum martyrum corpora Ambrosius Mediolani, per visum sibi monstrata, invenit?
question_en: The bodies of which martyrs, revealed to him through a vision, did Ambrose find at Milan?
derivation: The 'antistes' is Ambrose (named in 9.7.15). Through a vision he found the bodies of the martyrs Protasius and Gervasius ('martyrum corpora Protasii et Gervasii'), later moved to the Ambrosian basilica. Anchored to Ambrose + Milan; two-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book (the inventio of SS. Gervasius and Protasius).

author: Augustine
source_text: recordatus sum veridicos versus Ambrosii tui. tu es enim, deus, creator omnium, polique rector vestiens diem decoro lumine, noctem sopora gratia, artus solutos ut quies reddat laboris usui mentesque fessas allevet luctuque solvat anxios.
question: A quo auctore compositi sunt versus 'Deus creator omnium' quos Augustinus post matris suae mortem recordatus est?
question_en: By what author were the verses 'Deus creator omnium,' which Augustine recalled after his mother's death, composed?
derivation: Augustine recalls 'veridicos versus Ambrosii tui' beginning 'deus, creator omnium' — the Ambrosian hymn. Anchored to Augustine + Ambrose; single-name answer supported verbatim. Closed-book (a famous Ambrosian hymn). Source_text normalized: per-line quotation marks and a stray bracket stripped, hymn lines joined.

author: Augustine
source_text: fidelis promissor reddis Verecundo pro rure illo eius Cassiciaco, ubi ab aestu saeculi requievimus in te, amoenitatem sempiterne virentis paradisi tui.
question: Quo nomine appellabatur rus Verecundi ubi Augustinus cum suis post conversionem requievit?
question_en: By what name was the country estate of Verecundus, where Augustine and his companions rested after their conversion, called?
derivation: Verecundus's estate where Augustine's party retreated is named Cassiciacum ('pro rure illo eius Cassiciaco, ubi... requievimus'). Anchored to Verecundus + Augustine; single place-name answer (ablative 'Cassiciaco' in text, nom. Cassiciacum). Closed-book (the Cassiciacum retreat/dialogues are famous in Augustine's biography).

author: Caesar
source_text: Sic vocibus consulis, terrore praesentis exercitus, minis amicorum Pompei plerique compulsi inviti et coacti Scipionis sententiam sequuntur: uti ante certam diem Caesar exercitum dimittat; si non faciat, eum adversus rem publicam facturum videri. Intercedit M. Antonius, Q. Cassius, tribuni plebis.
question: Qui duo tribuni plebis sententiae, ut Caesar exercitum dimitteret, intercesserunt?
question_en: Which two tribunes of the plebs vetoed the motion that Caesar should disband his army?
derivation: Name fact anchored to the senate's decree that Caesar disband his army; the two named tribunes (Mark Antony and Q. Cassius Longinus) who interposed the veto are given verbatim ('Intercedit M. Antonius, Q. Cassius, tribuni plebis'). The veto and the tribunes' subsequent flight to Caesar are the iconic opening of the civil war; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Profugiunt statim ex urbe tribuni plebis seseque ad Caesarem conferunt. Is eo tempore erat Ravennae exspectabatque suis lenissimis postulatis responsa.
question: In quo oppido erat Caesar, cum tribuni plebis ex urbe profugientes ad eum se contulerunt?
question_en: In what town was Caesar when the tribunes of the plebs fled the city and came to him?
derivation: Place fact anchored to Caesar and the fleeing tribunes; locative answer supported verbatim by 'Is eo tempore erat Ravennae'. Caesar's position at Ravenna at the outbreak of the war is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Conclamant legionis XIII, quae aderat, milites—hanc enim initio tumultus evocaverat, reliquae nondum convenerant—sese paratos esse imperatoris sui tribunorumque plebis iniurias defendere.
question: Cuius legionis milites, quae sola initio tumultus aderat, se paratos esse Caesaris tribunorumque plebis iniurias defendere conclamaverunt?
question_en: The soldiers of which legion, the only one present at the start of the disturbance, shouted that they were ready to defend the wrongs done to Caesar and the tribunes of the plebs?
derivation: Number/name fact anchored to Caesar and the start of the war; answer (legio XIII) supported verbatim, including 'quae aderat' and 'reliquae nondum convenerant' (only the Thirteenth was present). The legion that crossed the Rubicon with Caesar; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Cognita militum voluntate Ariminum cum ea legione proficiscitur ibique tribunos plebis, qui ad eum profugerant, convenit.
question: In quod oppidum Caesar cum legione XIII primum profectus est, ubi tribunos plebis profugos convenit?
question_en: To which town did Caesar first advance with the Thirteenth Legion, where he met the fugitive tribunes of the plebs?
derivation: Place fact anchored to Caesar and the Thirteenth Legion; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Ariminum cum ea legione proficiscitur ibique tribunos plebis ... convenit'. Caesar's first seizure across the Rubicon; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Cum his ad Domitium Ahenobarbum Corfinium magnis itineribus pervenit Caesaremque adesse cum legionibus duabus nuntiat.
question: Ad quem Pompeianorum ducem Caesar Corfinium magnis itineribus pervenit?
question_en: Against which Pompeian commander did Caesar march to Corfinium by forced marches?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Corfinium and Caesar; single named answer supported verbatim by 'ad Domitium Ahenobarbum Corfinium ... pervenit' (the praenomen L. given at 1.23). Domitius Ahenobarbus, besieged at Corfinium and there pardoned by Caesar, is closed-book history.

author: Caesar
source_text: Pompeius his rebus cognitis, quae erant ad Corfinium gestae, Luceria proficiscitur Canusium atque inde Brundisium.
question: In quod oppidum maritimum Pompeius, cognitis rebus ad Corfinium gestis, Luceria per Canusium se recepit?
question_en: To which coastal town did Pompey withdraw, by way of Luceria and Canusium, once he learned of the events at Corfinium?
derivation: Place fact anchored to Pompey and Corfinium; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Luceria proficiscitur Canusium atque inde Brundisium'. Pompey's retreat to Brundisium is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Reperit consules Dyrrachium profectos cum magna parte exercitus, Pompeium remanere Brundisii cum cohortibus viginti.
question: Quo profectos esse consules Caesar, Brundisium cum legionibus perveniens, repperit?
question_en: Where had the consuls departed to, as Caesar found when he arrived at Brundisium with his legions?
derivation: Place fact anchored to the consuls, Brundisium, and Caesar; single answer supported verbatim by 'consules Dyrrachium profectos'. The consuls' crossing of the Adriatic to Greece is closed-book. Acc.+inf. 'profectos esse' under repperit.

author: Caesar
source_text: Mittit in Sardiniam cum legione una Valerium legatum, in Siciliam Curionem pro praetore cum legionibus duabus; eundem, cum Siciliam recepisset, protinus in Africam traducere exercitum iubet. Sardiniam obtinebat M. Cotta, Siciliam M. Cato; Africam sorte Tubero obtinere debebat.
question: Quis ex Pompeianis Siciliam obtinebat, quam Caesar Curionem occupare iussit?
question_en: Who held Sicily for the Pompeians, the province Caesar ordered Curio to seize?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Sicily and Curio; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Siciliam M. Cato [obtinebat]', with Curio sent there with two legions. Cato Uticensis abandoning Sicily before Curio is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Quibus effectis armatisque diebus XXX, a qua die materia caesa est, adductisque Massiliam his D. Brutum praeficit, C. Trebonium legatum ad oppugnationem Massiliae relinquit.
question: Quem legatum Caesar ad oppugnationem Massiliae reliquit?
question_en: Which legate did Caesar leave in charge of the siege of Massilia?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Massilia and Caesar; single named answer supported verbatim by 'C. Trebonium legatum ad oppugnationem Massiliae relinquit' (D. Brutus being set over the fleet). The siege of Massilia under Trebonius is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Afranius et Petreius et Varro, legati Pompei, quorum unus Hispaniam citeriorem tribus legionibus, alter ulteriorem a saltu Castulonensi ad Anam duabus legionibus, tertius ab Ana Vettonum agrum Lusitaniamque pari numero legionum optinebat.
question: Qui tres legati Pompei initio belli civilis Hispanias obtinebant?
question_en: Which three legates of Pompey held the Spanish provinces at the outbreak of the civil war?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Pompey and the Spanish provinces; the three named legates are given verbatim ('Afranius et Petreius et Varro, legati Pompei'). Pompey's Spanish command is closed-book; answer is the closed set of three.

author: Caesar
source_text: Quibus coactis celeriter Petreius per Vettones ad Afranium pervenit, constituuntque communi consilio bellum ad Ilerdam propter ipsius opportunitatem gerere.
question: Ad quod oppidum Afranius et Petreius communi consilio bellum gerere constituerunt?
question_en: At which town did Afranius and Petreius jointly decide to wage the war?
derivation: Place fact anchored to Afranius and Petreius; single named answer supported verbatim by 'bellum ad Ilerdam ... gerere'. The campaign of Ilerda is the central episode of Book I; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Caesar legiones in Hispaniam praemiserat VI, auxilia peditum V milia, equitum III milia.
question: Quot legiones Caesar in Hispaniam praemisit?
question_en: How many legions did Caesar send ahead into Spain?
derivation: Number fact anchored to Caesar and Spain; answer (VI = six) supported verbatim by 'legiones in Hispaniam praemiserat VI' and echoed at 1.85 ('sex legiones ... missas in Hispaniam'). Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Fabius finitimarum civitatum animos litteris nuntiisque temptabat. In Sicori flumine pontes effecerat duos distantes inter se milia passuum IIII.
question: In quo flumine apud Ilerdam C. Fabius, Caesaris legatus, duos pontes effecit?
question_en: In which river near Ilerda did Caesar's legate Gaius Fabius build two bridges?
derivation: Geography fact anchored to Fabius and Ilerda; single named answer supported verbatim by 'In Sicori flumine pontes effecerat duos'. The Sicoris (Segre) is the river of the Ilerda campaign; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Petreius atque Afranius cum stipendium ab legionibus paene seditione facta flagitarentur, cuius illi diem nondum venisse dicerent, Caesar ut cognosceret, postulatum est, eoque utrique, quod statuit, contenti fuerunt. Parte circiter tertia exercitus eo biduo dimissa duas legiones suas antecedere, reliquas subsequi iussit, ut non longo inter se spatio castra facerent, eique negotio Q. Fufium Calenum legatum praeficit. Hoc eius praescripto ex Hispania ad Varum flumen est iter factum, atque ibi reliqua pars exercitus dimissa est.
question: Ad quod flumen exercitus Afranii et Petreii in Hispania victus a Caesare dimissus est?
question_en: To which river was the defeated army of Afranius and Petreius led from Spain and disbanded?
derivation: Place/outcome fact anchored to Afranius and Petreius (named in the same paragraph) and Spain; single named answer supported verbatim by 'ex Hispania ad Varum flumen est iter factum, atque ibi reliqua pars exercitus dimissa est'. The surrender and disbandment of the Pompeian army in Spain is the climax of Book I; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Gallos ab Aquitanis Garumna flumen, a Belgis Matrona et Sequana dividit.
question: Quod flumen, ut Caesar scribit, Gallos ab Aquitanis dividit?
question_en: Which river, as Caesar writes, divides the Gauls from the Aquitani?
derivation: Geography fact of the famous opening chapter. Anchored to the Gauls, the Aquitani, and Caesar; single river answer supported verbatim by 'Gallos ab Aquitanis Garumna flumen ... dividit'. Closed-book staple of Latin geography.

author: Caesar
source_text: Apud Helvetios longe nobilissimus fuit et ditissimus Orgetorix.
question: Quis apud Helvetios longe nobilissimus ac ditissimus fuit?
question_en: Who was by far the noblest and richest man among the Helvetii?
derivation: Name fact anchored to the Helvetii; single named answer supported verbatim. Orgetorix is the well-known instigator of the Helvetian migration; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Pro multitudine autem hominum et pro gloria belli atque fortitudinis angustos se fines habere arbitrabantur, qui in longitudinem milia passuum CCXL, in latitudinem CLXXX patebant.
question: Quot milia passuum in longitudinem fines Helvetiorum patebant?
question_en: How many miles in length did the territory of the Helvetii extend?
derivation: Measure fact anchored to the Helvetii; number answer (CCXL = 240) supported verbatim, the width being CLXXX. The guidelines list exactly this kind of distance fact as a target.

author: Caesar
source_text: Id hoc facilius iis persuasit, quod undique loci natura Helvetii continentur: una ex parte flumine Rheno latissimo atque altissimo, qui agrum Helvetium a Germanis dividit; altera ex parte monte Iura altissimo, qui est inter Sequanos et Helvetios; tertia lacu Lemanno et flumine Rhodano, qui provinciam nostram ab Helvetiis dividit.
question: Qui mons inter Sequanos et Helvetios situs est?
question_en: Which mountain lies between the Sequani and the Helvetii?
derivation: Geography fact anchored to the Sequani and Helvetii; single answer supported verbatim by 'monte Iura altissimo, qui est inter Sequanos et Helvetios'. Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Itemque Dumnorigi Haeduo, fratri Diviciaci, qui eo tempore principatum in civitate obtinebat ac maxime plebi acceptus erat, ut idem conaretur persuadet eique filiam suam in matrimonium dat.
question: Cui Orgetorix filiam suam in matrimonium dedit?
question_en: To whom did Orgetorix give his daughter in marriage?
derivation: Relation fact anchored to Orgetorix; single named answer supported verbatim by 'eique filiam suam in matrimonium dat' (the antecedent being Dumnorix). Dumnorix is a major figure of Book 1; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Caesar, quod memoria tenebat L. Cassium consulem occisum exercitumque eius ab Helvetiis pulsum et sub iugum missum, concedendum non putabat.
question: Quem consulem Romanum Helvetii antea occiderant eiusque exercitum sub iugum miserant?
question_en: Which Roman consul had the Helvetii earlier killed, and sent his army under the yoke?
derivation: Historical name fact anchored to the Helvetii and a consul; single named answer supported verbatim. The defeat of L. Cassius (107 BC) is closed-book history echoed again in 1.12.

author: Caesar
source_text: Interea ea legione quam secum habebat militibusque, qui ex provincia convenerant, a lacu Lemanno, qui in flumen Rhodanum influit, ad montem Iuram, qui fines Sequanorum ab Helvetiis dividit, milia passuum XVIIII murum in altitudinem pedum sedecim fossamque perducit.
question: Quot milia passuum longum murum Caesar a lacu Lemanno ad montem Iuram perduxit?
question_en: How many miles long was the wall Caesar built from Lake Geneva to the Jura?
derivation: Number/engineering fact anchored to Caesar, Lake Leman, and the Jura; answer (XVIIII = 19) supported verbatim (the height being sixteen feet). Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Flumen est Arar, quod per fines Haeduorum et Sequanorum in Rhodanum influit, incredibili lenitate, ita ut oculis in utram partem fluat iudicari non possit.
question: In quod flumen Ararim influere Caesar scribit?
question_en: Into which river does Caesar write the Arar flows?
derivation: Geography fact anchored to the Arar (Saone); single answer supported verbatim by 'in Rhodanum influit'. Indirect statement (Ararim influere) governed by scribit; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Is pagus appellabatur Tigurinus; nam omnis civitas Helvetia in quattuor pagos divisa est. Hic pagus unus, cum domo exisset, patrum nostrorum memoria L. Cassium consulem interfecerat et eius exercitum sub iugum miserat.
question: Quo nomine appellabatur pagus Helvetius qui L. Cassium consulem interfecerat?
question_en: What was the name of the Helvetian canton that had killed the consul Lucius Cassius?
derivation: Name fact anchored to the Helvetii and to Cassius; single named answer supported verbatim ('Is pagus appellabatur Tigurinus' + 'L. Cassium consulem interfecerat'). Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Legatos ad eum mittunt; cuius legationis Divico princeps fuit, qui bello Cassiano dux Helvetiorum fuerat.
question: Quis dux Helvetiorum bello Cassiano fuerat et postea legationi ad Caesarem missae praefuit?
question_en: Who had been the leader of the Helvetii in the Cassian war and later headed the embassy to Caesar?
derivation: Name fact doubly anchored (Helvetii, the Cassian war, Caesar); single named answer supported verbatim by 'Divico princeps fuit, qui bello Cassiano dux Helvetiorum fuerat'. Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Qui summo magistratui praeerat, quem vergobretum appellant Haedui, qui creatur annuus et vitae necisque in suos habet potestatem.
question: Quo nomine Haedui summum magistratum suum appellant?
question_en: By what name do the Haedui call their supreme magistrate?
derivation: Institution/custom fact anchored to the Haedui; single named answer supported verbatim by 'quem vergobretum appellant Haedui'. A distinctive named office (annual, with power of life and death); closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: A Bibracte, oppido Haeduorum longe maximo et copiosissimo, non amplius milibus passuum XVIII aberat.
question: Quod oppidum Haeduorum longe maximum et copiosissimum fuisse Caesar scribit?
question_en: Which town does Caesar write was by far the largest and richest of the Haedui?
derivation: Place fact anchored to the Haedui; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Bibracte, oppido Haeduorum longe maximo et copiosissimo'. Indirect statement (fuisse) under scribit; the iconic Aeduan oppidum, closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: In castris Helvetiorum tabulae repertae sunt litteris Graecis confectae et ad Caesarem relatae, quibus in tabulis nominatim ratio confecta erat, qui numerus domo exisset eorum qui arma ferre possent, et item separatim, quot pueri, senes mulieresque.
question: Quibus litteris tabulae in castris Helvetiorum repertae confectae erant?
question_en: In what script were the tablets found in the camp of the Helvetii written?
derivation: A striking, much-cited fact anchored to the Helvetian camp; single answer supported verbatim by 'tabulae ... litteris Graecis confectae'. Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ariovistus, rex Germanorum, in eorum finibus consedisset tertiamque partem agri Sequani, qui esset optimus totius Galliae, occupavisset.
question: Quis erat rex Germanorum qui in finibus Sequanorum consedit?
question_en: Who was the king of the Germani who settled in the territory of the Sequani?
derivation: Name fact anchored to the Germani and the Sequani; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Ariovistus, rex Germanorum, in eorum finibus consedisset'. Ariovistus is the central antagonist of Book 1; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Nuntiatum est ei Ariovistum cum suis omnibus copiis ad occupandum Vesontionem, quod est oppidum maximum Sequanorum, contendere.
question: Quod oppidum, Sequanorum maximum, Ariovistus occupare contendit?
question_en: Which town, the largest of the Sequani, did Ariovistus hasten to seize?
derivation: Place fact anchored to the Sequani and Ariovistus; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Vesontionem, quod est oppidum maximum Sequanorum'. Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Apud Germanos ea consuetudo esset ut matres familiae eorum sortibus et vaticinationibus declararent utrum proelium committi ex usu esset necne; eas ita dicere: non esse fas Germanos superare, si ante novam lunam proelio contendissent.
question: Ante quid Germanos vincere fas non esse matres familiae declarabant?
question_en: Before what did the German matrons declare it was not right (fas) for the Germani to win?
derivation: Ethnographic custom fact anchored to the Germani; short answer supported verbatim by 'non esse fas Germanos superare, si ante novam lunam proelio contendissent'. Distinctive and closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: crebri ad eum rumores adferebantur litterisque item Labieni certior fiebat omnes Belgas, quam tertiam esse Galliae partem dixeramus, contra populum Romanum coniurare obsidesque inter se dare.
question: Quam Galliae partem Belgas esse Caesar scribit?
question_en: Which part of Gaul does Caesar say the Belgae are?
derivation: The famous opening fact echoed from BG 1.1: the Belgae are the third of the three parts of Gaul. Anchored to the Belgae and Caesar; single answer supported verbatim by 'quam tertiam esse Galliae partem'. Indirect statement (Belgas esse partem) under scribit; closed-book staple of Latin geography.

author: Caesar
source_text: crebri ad eum rumores adferebantur litterisque item Labieni certior fiebat omnes Belgas, quam tertiam esse Galliae partem dixeramus, contra populum Romanum coniurare obsidesque inter se dare.
question: Contra quem populum omnes Belgas coniurare Caesar litteris Labieni certior factus est?
question_en: Against what people was Caesar informed, by letters from Labienus, that all the Belgae were conspiring?
derivation: The opening fact of Book II. Anchored to the Belgae, Labienus, and Caesar; single answer supported verbatim by 'omnes Belgas ... contra populum Romanum coniurare'. Indirect statement (Belgas coniurare) under certior factus est; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Remi, qui proximi Galliae ex Belgis sunt, ad eum legatos Iccium et Andebrogium, primos civitatis, miserunt, qui dicerent se suaque omnia in fidem atque potestatem populi Romani permittere, neque se cum reliquis Belgis consensisse neque contra populum Romanum coniurasse.
question: Qui populus Belgarum primus legatos ad Caesarem misit seque in fidem populi Romani permisit?
question_en: Which people of the Belgae was the first to send legates to Caesar and to commit itself to the protection of the Roman people?
derivation: Anchored to the Belgae and Caesar; the Remi alone broke from the coalition and submitted first ('Remi ... ad eum legatos ... miserunt, qui dicerent se ... in fidem atque potestatem populi Romani permittere'). The Remi's early alliance is a staple of BG II; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Suessiones suos esse finitimos; fines latissimos feracissimosque agros possidere. Apud eos fuisse regem nostra etiam memoria Diviciacum, totius Galliae potentissimum, qui cum magnae partis harum regionum, tum etiam Britanniae imperium obtinuerit; nunc esse regem Galbam: ad hunc propter iustitiam prudentiamque summam totius belli omnium voluntate deferri.
question: Cui Suessionum regi summa totius belli a Belgis omnium voluntate delata est?
question_en: To which king of the Suessiones was the supreme command of the whole war entrusted by the unanimous wish of the Belgae?
derivation: Named-leader fact anchored to the Suessiones and the Belgic coalition; Galba is the Belgic commander-in-chief ('nunc esse regem Galbam: ad hunc ... summam totius belli omnium voluntate deferri'). His kingship is confirmed at 2.13, where his two sons are given as hostages. Single named answer; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: totidem Nervios, qui maxime feri inter ipsos habeantur longissimeque absint;
question: Qui populus inter Belgas maxime ferus habebatur?
question_en: Which people was reckoned the fiercest among the Belgae?
derivation: Anchored to the Belgae; the Nervii are reckoned the fiercest of them ('Nervios, qui maxime feri inter ipsos habeantur'), a judgement echoed at 2.15 ('esse homines feros magnaeque virtutis'). One of the best-known characterizations in BG II; closed-book, single named answer.

author: Caesar
source_text: Iccius Remus, summa nobilitate et gratia inter suos, qui tum oppido praeerat, unus ex iis qui legati de pace ad Caesarem venerant, nuntium ad eum mittit, nisi subsidium sibi submittatur, sese diutius sustinere non posse.
question: Quis Remus summae nobilitatis, qui oppido a Belgis obsesso praeerat, nuntium de subsidio ad Caesarem misit?
question_en: Which Reman of the highest nobility, who commanded the town besieged by the Belgae, sent a message asking Caesar for relief?
derivation: Named-leader fact anchored to the Remi, the Belgic siege, and Caesar. Iccius commanded the besieged town (Bibrax, named earlier in 2.6) and sent to Caesar for relief ('Iccius Remus ... qui tum oppido praeerat ... nuntium ad eum mittit'); he was also one of the Reman envoys of 2.3. Single named answer; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Eorum fines Nervii attingebant. Quorum de natura moribusque Caesar cum quaereret, sic reperiebat: nullum esse aditum ad eos mercatoribus; nihil pati vini reliquarumque rerum ad luxuriam pertinentium inferri, quod his rebus relanguescere animos eorum et remitti virtutem existimarent.
question: Quam potionem Nervii in fines suos inferri non patiebantur, ne animi eorum relanguescerent?
question_en: What drink did the Nervii not allow to be imported into their territory, lest their spirits be weakened?
derivation: Ethnographic custom anchored to the Nervii; they admitted no merchants and allowed no wine or luxuries to be imported ('nihil pati vini ... inferri, quod his rebus relanguescere animos eorum ... existimarent'). A famous Nervian custom; closed-book, short answer.

author: Caesar
source_text: Cum per eorum fines triduum iter fecisset, inveniebat ex captivis Sabim flumen a castris suis non amplius milibus passuum X abesse; trans id flumen omnes Nervios consedisse adventumque ibi Romanorum expectare una cum Atrebatibus et Viromanduis, finitimis suis.
question: Ad quod flumen omnes Nervios consedisse Caesar ex captivis cognovit?
question_en: At which river did Caesar learn from prisoners that all the Nervii had encamped?
derivation: Geography/battle fact anchored to the Nervii; the river Sabis (Sambre), site of the famous battle, supported verbatim by 'trans id flumen omnes Nervios consedisse'. Single named answer; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: et in commemoranda civitatis calamitate ex DC ad tres senatores, ex hominum milibus LX vix ad D, qui arma ferre possent, sese redactos esse dixerunt.
question: Ex sescentis senatoribus ad quot senatores se redactos esse Nervii post proelium dixerunt?
question_en: From six hundred senators, to how many did the Nervii say they had been reduced after the battle?
derivation: Number fact anchored to the Nervii (the 'civitas' of ch. 28, nearly annihilated at the Sabis); after the battle they declared themselves reduced from 600 senators to 3 ('ex DC ad tres senatores ... sese redactos esse'). The near-destruction of the Nervii is iconic; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ipsi erant ex Cimbris Teutonisque prognati, qui, cum iter in provinciam nostram atque Italiam facerent, iis impedimentis quae secum agere ac portare non poterant citra flumen Rhenum depositis custodiam ex suis ac praesidium VI milia hominum una reliquerant.
question: Ex quibus gentibus Atuatucos prognatos esse Caesar tradit?
question_en: From which peoples does Caesar relate the Aduatuci were descended?
answer_en: From the Cimbri and the Teutoni.
derivation: Origin fact anchored to the Aduatuci ('Ipsi' = the Atuatuci, subject of ch. 29); descended from the Cimbri and Teutoni, supported verbatim by 'Ipsi erant ex Cimbris Teutonisque prognati'. Indirect statement (prognatos esse) under tradit; the Aduatuci's Cimbric descent is a well-known BG II fact; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ipsi erant ex Cimbris Teutonisque prognati, qui, cum iter in provinciam nostram atque Italiam facerent, iis impedimentis quae secum agere ac portare non poterant citra flumen Rhenum depositis custodiam ex suis ac praesidium VI milia hominum una reliquerant. Hi post eorum obitum multos annos a finitimis exagitati, cum alias bellum inferrent, alias inlatum defenderent, consensu eorum omnium pace facta hunc sibi domicilio locum delegerant.
question: Quot hominum milia Cimbri Teutonique citra Rhenum custodiae causa reliquerunt, unde Atuatuci orti sunt?
question_en: How many thousand men did the Cimbri and Teutoni leave as a guard on the near side of the Rhine, from whom the Aduatuci sprang?
derivation: Number/origin fact anchored to the Cimbri, Teutoni, and the Aduatuci; the 6,000 men left as a garrison ('VI milia hominum una reliquerant') became the Aduatuci ('Hi ... hunc sibi domicilio locum delegerant'). Single number answer supported verbatim; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Postridie eius diei refractis portis, cum iam defenderet nemo, atque intromissis militibus nostris, sectionem eius oppidi universam Caesar vendidit. Ab iis qui emerant capitum numerus ad eum relatus est milium LIII.
question: Quot capitum milia ex oppido Atuatucorum vendito ab emptoribus Caesari renuntiata sunt?
question_en: How many thousand persons from the sold town of the Aduatuci were reported back to Caesar by the buyers?
derivation: The headline figure of the Aduatuci episode, anchored to the Aduatuci ('eius oppidi' = their stronghold of ch. 33); after Caesar sold the whole town, the buyers reported 53,000 heads ('capitum numerus ad eum relatus est milium LIII'). Single number answer supported verbatim; one of the most-cited figures in BG, closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ob easque res ex litteris Caesaris dierum XV supplicatio decreta est, quod ante id tempus accidit nulli.
question: Quot dierum supplicatio ob res a Caesare in Belgis gestas Romae decreta est?
question_en: A thanksgiving of how many days was decreed at Rome for the deeds Caesar accomplished among the Belgae?
derivation: Historical fact anchored to Caesar; a 15-day supplicatio was decreed for these achievements, an unprecedented honour ('dierum XV supplicatio decreta est, quod ante id tempus accidit nulli'). Single number answer supported verbatim; the first 15-day thanksgiving ever voted, closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ea quae secuta est hieme, qui fuit annus Cn. Pompeio, M. Crasso consulibus, Usipetes Germani et item Tencteri magna cum multitudine hominum flumen Rhenum transierunt, non longe a mari, quo Rhenus influit.
question: Quae duae gentes Germanorum flumen Rhenum, Cn. Pompeio et M. Crasso consulibus, transierunt?
question_en: Which two German peoples crossed the river Rhine in the consulship of Cn. Pompeius and M. Crassus?
derivation: Opening fact of Book 4, anchored to the consular year (55 BC) and the Rhine. Two named peoples whose migration and destruction frame the book; answer supported verbatim by 'Usipetes Germani et item Tencteri ... flumen Rhenum transierunt'. Closed-book, the iconic Germanic crossing of BG 4.

author: Caesar
source_text: Sueborum gens est longe maxima et bellicosissima Germanorum omnium.
question: Quae gens, ut Caesar scribit, omnium Germanorum longe maxima et bellicosissima est?
question_en: Which people, as Caesar writes, is by far the largest and most warlike of all the Germans?
derivation: Ethnographic superlative fact anchored to the Germans; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Sueborum gens est longe maxima et bellicosissima Germanorum omnium'. The Suebi are the recurrent Germanic power of the book; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Nostri ad unum omnes incolumes, perpaucis vulneratis, ex tanti belli timore, cum hostium numerus capitum CCCCXXX milium fuisset, se in castra receperunt.
question: Quot milia hominum fuisse hostium numerum Caesar scribit, cum Usipetes et Tencteri ad confluentem Mosae et Rheni deleti sunt?
question_en: How many thousand men does Caesar say the enemy numbered when the Usipetes and Tencteri were destroyed at the confluence of the Meuse and the Rhine?
derivation: Number fact anchored to the destroyed Germans (Usipetes and Tencteri); answer (CCCCXXX milia = 430,000) supported verbatim by 'hostium numerus capitum CCCCXXX milium fuisset'. A much-cited total; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ubii autem, qui uni ex Transrhenanis ad Caesarem legatos miserant, amicitiam fecerant, obsides dederant, magnopere orabant ut sibi auxilium ferret, quod graviter ab Suebis premerentur.
question: Quae gens Germanorum una ex Transrhenanis ad Caesarem legatos miserat eique amicitiam fecerat?
question_en: Which German people, alone of those beyond the Rhine, had sent envoys to Caesar and made friendship with him?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Caesar and the peoples across the Rhine; single answer supported verbatim by 'Ubii ... qui uni ex Transrhenanis ad Caesarem legatos miserant, amicitiam fecerant'. The Ubii's appeal motivates the Rhine bridge; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Diebus X, quibus materia coepta erat comportari, omni opere effecto exercitus traducitur.
question: Quot diebus pons Caesaris in Rheno effectus est, ut ipse scribit?
question_en: In how many days was Caesar's bridge over the Rhine built, as he himself writes?
derivation: Number fact about the famous Rhine bridge, anchored to Caesar and the Rhine; answer (decem) supported verbatim by 'Diebus X, quibus materia coepta erat comportari, omni opere effecto exercitus traducitur'. The speed of the timber bridge is the iconic detail; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: diebus omnino XVIII trans Rhenum consumptis, satis et ad laudem et ad utilitatem profectum arbitratus se in Galliam recepit pontemque rescidit.
question: Quot omnino dies Caesar trans Rhenum consumpsit, antequam in Galliam rediret pontemque rescinderet?
question_en: How many days in all did Caesar spend across the Rhine before returning to Gaul and breaking down the bridge?
derivation: Number fact anchored to Caesar and his first crossing into Germany; answer (XVIII = 18) supported verbatim by 'diebus omnino XVIII trans Rhenum consumptis ... se in Galliam recepit pontemque rescidit'. Closed-book; the length of the first Roman stay in Germany.

author: Caesar
source_text: Exigua parte aestatis reliqua Caesar, etsi in his locis, quod omnis Gallia ad septentriones vergit, maturae sunt hiemes, tamen in Britanniam proficisci contendit, quod omnibus fere Gallicis bellis hostibus nostris inde subministrata auxilia intellegebat.
question: In quam insulam Caesar exigua parte aestatis reliqua proficisci contendit?
question_en: To which island did Caesar hasten to set out when only a small part of the summer remained?
derivation: Place fact marking Caesar's first expedition to Britain, anchored to Caesar and the time of year; answer supported verbatim by 'tamen in Britanniam proficisci contendit'. The first Roman crossing to Britain is a closed-book landmark.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ad haec cognoscenda, prius quam periculum faceret, idoneum esse arbitratus C. Volusenum cum navi longa praemittit. Huic mandat ut exploratis omnibus rebus ad se quam primum revertatur.
question: Quem Caesar cum navi longa praemisit ut Britanniam ante adventum suum exploraret?
question_en: Whom did Caesar send ahead with a warship to reconnoiter Britain before his own arrival?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Caesar and the reconnaissance of Britain; single named answer supported verbatim by 'C. Volusenum cum navi longa praemittit'. The first scouting of Britain; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: et cum iis una Commium, quem ipse Atrebatibus superatis regem ibi constituerat, cuius et virtutem et consilium probabat et quem sibi fidelem esse arbitrabatur cuiusque auctoritas in his regionibus magni habebatur, mittit.
question: Cui genti Caesar Commium regem constituerat, quem in Britanniam praemisit?
question_en: Over which people had Caesar made Commius king, the man he sent ahead to Britain?
derivation: Name/relation fact anchored to Commius and Caesar; answer supported verbatim by 'Commium, quem ipse Atrebatibus superatis regem ibi constituerat'. Commius the Atrebatian is a recurring named figure; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Navibus circiter LXXX onerariis coactis contractisque, quot satis esse ad duas transportandas legiones existimabat, quod praeterea navium longarum habebat quaestori, legatis praefectisque distribuit.
question: Quot legiones Caesar primo in Britanniam transportare statuit, navibus circiter LXXX onerariis coactis?
question_en: How many legions did Caesar decide to transport to Britain on his first expedition, having gathered about 80 transport ships?
derivation: Number fact anchored to Caesar and the first British expedition; answer (duae legiones) supported verbatim by 'quot satis esse ad duas transportandas legiones existimabat'. The small two-legion force of 55 BC is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Atque nostris militibus cunctantibus, maxime propter altitudinem maris, qui X legionis aquilam gerebat, obtestatus deos, ut ea res legioni feliciter eveniret, 'desilite', inquit, 'milites, nisi vultis aquilam hostibus prodere; ego certe meum rei publicae atque imperatori officium praestitero.' Hoc cum voce magna dixisset, se ex navi proiecit atque in hostes aquilam ferre coepit.
question: Cuius legionis aquilifer primus in mare se proiecit, milites ad desiliendum cohortans, cum Romani in Britanniam egrederentur?
question_en: The standard-bearer of which legion first threw himself into the sea, urging the soldiers to leap down, as the Romans were landing in Britain?
derivation: Name/number fact anchored to the British landing and a named legion; answer (decima) supported verbatim by 'qui X legionis aquilam gerebat ... se ex navi proiecit atque in hostes aquilam ferre coepit'. The aquilifer of the Tenth at the British landing is a famous, closed-book scene.

author: Caesar
source_text: His rebus gestis ex litteris Caesaris dierum XX supplicatio a senatu decreta est.
question: Quot dierum supplicationem senatus ex litteris Caesaris decrevit, postquam ille Rhenum transiit et in Britanniam navigavit?
question_en: How many days' thanksgiving did the senate decree on Caesar's dispatch, after he had crossed the Rhine and sailed to Britain?
derivation: Number/institution fact anchored to the senate and Caesar's campaigns of 55 BC; answer (XX = 20) supported verbatim by 'dierum XX supplicatio a senatu decreta est'. The closing public honor of the book; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Eo cum venisset, maiores iam undique in eum locum copiae Britannorum convenerant summa imperi bellique administrandi communi consilio permissa Cassivellauno, cuius fines a maritimis civitatibus flumen dividit, quod appellatur Tamesis, a mari circiter milia passuum LXXX. Huic superiore tempore cum reliquis civitatibus continentia bella intercesserant; sed nostro adventu permoti Britanni hunc toti bello imperioque praefecerant.
question: Cui Britanni summam imperi bellique administrandi communi consilio permiserunt?
question_en: To whom did the Britons by common counsel entrust the supreme command and conduct of the war?
derivation: Name fact anchored to the Britons; single named answer supported verbatim by 'summa imperi bellique administrandi communi consilio permissa Cassivellauno' and 'hunc toti bello imperioque praefecerant'. Cassivellaunus, the British supreme commander against Caesar's second expedition, is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: summa imperi bellique administrandi communi consilio permissa Cassivellauno, cuius fines a maritimis civitatibus flumen dividit, quod appellatur Tamesis, a mari circiter milia passuum LXXX.
question: Quod flumen, ut Caesar scribit, fines Cassivellauni a maritimis civitatibus dividit?
question_en: Which river, as Caesar writes, divides the territory of Cassivellaunus from the maritime states?
derivation: Geography fact anchored to Cassivellaunus and Caesar; single river answer supported verbatim by 'cuius fines a maritimis civitatibus flumen dividit, quod appellatur Tamesis'. The Thames is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Haec civitas longe plurimum totius Galliae equitatu valet magnasque habet copias peditum Rhenumque, ut supra demonstravimus, tangit. In ea civitate duo de principatu inter se contendebant, Indutiomarus et Cingetorix.
question: Qui duo apud Treveros de principatu inter se contendebant?
question_en: Which two men contended with each other for the chieftaincy among the Treveri?
derivation: Name/relation fact anchored to the Treveri (the 'civitas' of 5.3, named throughout 5.3-4); two named answers supported verbatim by 'In ea civitate duo de principatu inter se contendebant, Indutiomarus et Cingetorix'. Both are major figures of the Treveran revolt; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: At omnium impeditis animis Dumnorix cum equitibus Aeduorum a castris insciente Caesare domum discedere coepit. Qua re nuntiata Caesar intermissa profectione atque omnibus rebus postpositis magnam partem equitatus ad eum insequendum mittit retrahique imperat; si vim faciat neque pareat, interfici iubet, nihil hunc se absente pro sano facturum arbitratus, qui praesentis imperium neglexisset. Ille enim revocatus resistere ac se manu defendere suorumque fidem implorare coepit, saepe clamitans liberum se liberaeque esse civitatis. Illi, ut erat imperatum, circumsistunt hominem atque interficiunt.
question: Quis Aeduus, qui se liberae civitatis liberum esse clamitabat, iussu Caesaris ab equitibus interfectus est?
question_en: Which Aeduan, who kept shouting that he was a free man of a free state, was killed by the cavalry on Caesar's order?
derivation: Name fact anchored to the Aedui and Caesar; single named answer supported verbatim by 'Dumnorix ... domum discedere coepit ... clamitans liberum se liberaeque esse civitatis. Illi ... interficiunt'. Dumnorix is a major figure (also Book 1); his death is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Alterum vergit ad Hispaniam atque occidentem solem; qua ex parte est Hibernia, dimidio minor, ut aestimatur, quam Britannia, sed pari spatio transmissus atque ex Gallia est in Britanniam. In hoc medio cursu est insula, quae appellatur Mona.
question: Quae insula, ut Caesar tradit, medio in cursu inter Britanniam et Hiberniam sita est?
question_en: Which island, as Caesar reports, lies midway in the passage between Britain and Ireland?
derivation: Geography fact anchored to Britannia and Hibernia; single named answer supported verbatim by 'In hoc medio cursu est insula, quae appellatur Mona'. Caesar's island Mona is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Omnes vero se Britanni vitro inficiunt, quod caeruleum efficit colorem, atque hoc horridiores sunt in pugna aspectu.
question: Qua re se omnes Britanni inficiunt, quae caeruleum efficit colorem?
question_en: With what do all the Britons stain themselves, the substance that produces a blue color?
derivation: Ethnographic custom fact anchored to the Britons; single answer supported verbatim by 'Omnes vero se Britanni vitro inficiunt, quod caeruleum efficit colorem'. The Britons' blue woad is a famous closed-book detail.

author: Caesar
source_text: Interim Trinobantes, prope firmissima earum regionum civitas, ex qua Mandubracius adulescens Caesaris fidem secutus ad eum in continentem Galliam venerat, cuius pater in ea civitate regnum obtinuerat interfectusque erat a Cassivellauno, ipse fuga mortem vitaverat.
question: Quis adulescens Trinobantum, cuius pater a Cassivellauno interfectus erat, Caesaris fidem secutus est?
question_en: Which young man of the Trinobantes, whose father had been killed by Cassivellaunus, sought Caesar's protection?
derivation: Name/relation fact anchored to the Trinobantes and Cassivellaunus; single named answer supported verbatim by 'ex qua Mandubracius adulescens Caesaris fidem secutus ... cuius pater ... interfectusque erat a Cassivellauno'. Closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Vnam legionem, quam proxime trans Padum conscripserat, et cohortes V in Eburones, quorum pars maxima est inter Mosam ac Rhenum, qui sub imperio Ambiorigis et Catuvolci erant, misit.
question: Inter quae duo flumina partem maximam Eburonum esse Caesar scribit?
question_en: Between which two rivers does Caesar write the greater part of the Eburones lies?
answer_en: Between the Meuse (Mosa) and the Rhine.
derivation: Geography fact anchored to the Eburones and Caesar; answer supported verbatim by 'in Eburones, quorum pars maxima est inter Mosam ac Rhenum'. Indirect statement under scribit; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Vnam legionem, quam proxime trans Padum conscripserat, et cohortes V in Eburones, quorum pars maxima est inter Mosam ac Rhenum, qui sub imperio Ambiorigis et Catuvolci erant, misit. Eis militibus Quintum Titurium Sabinum et Lucium Aurunculeium Cottam legatos praeesse iussit.
question: Quos duos legatos Caesar legioni in Eburones missae praeesse iussit?
answer: Quintum Titurium Sabinum et Lucium Aurunculeium Cottam.
question_en: Which two legates did Caesar place in charge of the legion sent among the Eburones?
answer_en: Quintus Titurius Sabinus and Lucius Aurunculeius Cotta.
derivation: Name fact anchored to Caesar and the legion among the Eburones; two named answers supported verbatim by 'Quintum Titurium Sabinum et Lucium Aurunculeium Cottam legatos praeesse iussit'. These are the two legates destroyed in Ambiorix's ambush; closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Ex quibus unam in Morinos ducendam Gaio Fabio legato dedit, alteram in Nervios Quinto Ciceroni, tertiam in Esubios Lucio Roscio.
question: Cui legato Caesar legionem in Nervios ducendam dedit?
question_en: To which legate did Caesar give the legion to lead among the Nervii?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Caesar and the Nervii; single named answer supported verbatim by 'alteram in Nervios Quinto Ciceroni'. Quintus Cicero (brother of the orator), whose winter camp among the Nervii was besieged and relieved by Caesar, is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Diebus circiter XV, quibus in hiberna ventum est, initium repentini tumultus ac defectionis ortum est ab Ambiorige et Catuvolco.
question: A quibus ducibus Eburonum initium repentini tumultus ac defectionis ortum est?
question_en: From which leaders of the Eburones did the sudden uprising and revolt begin?
derivation: Name fact anchored to the Eburones (whose chiefs they are, 5.24); two named answers supported verbatim by 'initium repentini tumultus ac defectionis ortum est ab Ambiorige et Catuvolco'. Ambiorix's revolt is closed-book.

author: Caesar
source_text: Erant in ea legione fortissimi viri, centuriones, qui primis ordinibus appropinquarent, Titus Pullo et Lucius Vorenus. Hi perpetuas inter se controversias habebant, quinam anteferretur, omnibusque annis de locis summis simultatibus contendebant.
question: Qui duo fortissimi centuriones in legione Ciceronis de locis summis perpetuo inter se contendebant?
question_en: Which two very brave centurions in Cicero's legion perpetually competed with each other for the top ranks?
derivation: Name fact anchored to Cicero's besieged legion (the 'ea legio' of 5.39-44); two named answers supported verbatim by 'centuriones ... Titus Pullo et Lucius Vorenus. Hi perpetuas inter se controversias habebant'. The rival centurions are a celebrated closed-book episode.

author: Caesar
